source: Lawsen (2025) The Illusion of the Illusion of Thinking (comment on Shojaee et al.)
finding: Rebuts the collapse claim: Hanoi failures coincide with output-token caps, and River Crossing instances with N>=6 actors and boat capacity 3 are unsolvable, so scoring them as failures is wrong. Asking for a Lua function instead of a full move list gave very high accuracy at 15 disks.
numbers: Hanoi N=15 as function: o3, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude Opus 4, Gemini 2.5, each under 5,000 tokens; accuracy only described as 'very high', 'preliminary', no counts. Author estimate 10 tokens per move (corrected in v2 from an earlier 5).
quote: Models receive zero scores not for reasoning failures, but for correctly recognizing unsolvable problems.
limits: Short comment, no systematic table; it shows the format was a problem, not that long procedures are solved. Does not re-run the other puzzles.
agent_relevance: Do not cite collapse points as reasoning limits. Give the agent a route to emit a procedure (code) instead of a long enumeration, and check solvability before scoring.

source: Song, Yue & Zhang (2025) Thinking Isn't an Illusion: overcoming the limitations of reasoning models via tool augmentations
finding: With a Python interpreter (program-of-thought) the reasoning models beat their non-reasoning twins on Apple's puzzles, and Hanoi is solved to N=13. Checker Jumping stays at 0 for N>=3 in every setting.
numbers: Each cell 5 runs only. DeepSeek-R1 with PoT about 80% on River Crossing and Blocks World; DeepSeek-V3 near 0 on River Crossing; Hanoi with PoT 5/5 at N=11 and 13 for DeepSeek-V3, R1, Qwen3, Qwen3-Thinking. Direct prompting Hanoi N=11,13: 0/5.
limits: Five trials per cell; table columns garbled in the PDF text so single cells are uncertain; models are DeepSeek and Qwen, not frontier closed models. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Tools turn a collapse into a pass for rule-driven puzzles. A code-execution operator is the cheapest rescue for long procedural tasks.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: Scaffold on versus off on a perturbed form. Irrelevant sentences cut accuracy; self-consistency and an instruction to ignore irrelevant text each help, and the best scaffolds still leave most base problems unsolved consistently.
numbers: code-davinci-002, GSM-IC-4K, exemplars without irrelevant context. Micro/macro accuracy: CoT 72.4/6.0; CoT+instruction 77.8/15.0; Least-to-Most 77.5/18.0 -> with instruction 80.6/25.0; CoT+SC 88.1/30.0; LTM+SC 93.4/45.0; Program 54.4/5.0; 0-CoT 29.0/1.0. Macro = share of base problems solved for every distractor variant.
quote: feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions
limits: Old models (code-davinci-002, text-davinci-003). Scaffold effects are on distractors only, not on counterfactual rules. Macro accuracy still at most 45% in the best case.
agent_relevance: Scaffolds help on perturbed variants but do not remove the gap. Vote plus a targeted instruction gave the largest robust gain.

source: Shi et al. (2023) GSM-IC, generic versus targeted instruction
finding: A generic instruction of similar form ('Solve grade school math problems.') did not significantly improve results; only the instruction naming the irrelevant-information problem made the difference.
numbers: Text states the generic instruction alone does not significantly improve; GSM-IC-4K, code-davinci-002. On clean GSM8K dev, CoT 59.3 vs 60.3 with the ignore-irrelevance instruction (no harm on clean problems).
quote: it is the instruction 'Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.' that makes the difference
limits: Exact numbers for the generic-instruction arm were not recoverable from the PDF table; one model family; one task.
agent_relevance: A working equal-style active control for scaffold tests: same form and tone, no task-relevant content. Use it as the placebo arm.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Reordering premises hurts, but the study runs zero-shot with greedy decoding and has no scaffold-on arm, so it cannot say whether scaffolds fix it.
numbers: R-GSM 220 reordered pairs, original vs reordered: GPT-4-turbo 94.1 vs 85.0; PaLM 2-L 86.4 vs 79.5; Gemini 1.0 Pro 80.5 vs 69.1; GPT-3.5-turbo 67.3 vs 51.8. Among problems solved originally: GPT-4-turbo 89.9, PaLM 2-L 87.9, Gemini 74.6, GPT-3.5 64.9. Deduction: forward order 96.5% for GPT-4-turbo; drops over 30 points for some models; Gemini 1.0 Pro below 25% in worst orders.
limits: Zero-shot, no CoT or voting arm. The 20-40+ point drop holds for logic; on R-GSM the drop is 9-15 points for the models above.
agent_relevance: K10 was too strong for math: 20-40 points is logic, 9-15 points is R-GSM. Gap 3 stays open for premise order: a scaffold-on arm is missing.

source: Li et al. (2024) GSM-Plus: robustness benchmark for math solvers
finding: Eight perturbation types; prompting variants raise accuracy on both GSM8K and perturbed sets. A compositional prompt (iterative subgoal plus verify) beat least-to-most by 3.4 points on GSM8K and 4.7 on GSM-Plus (GPT-3.5-Turbo). One perturbation column stayed lowest for CoT and LTM.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo, Table 5 rows: COT, LTM, COMP, COT+SC (5 samples), COMP+SC. In the lowest column (probably critical thinking, header lost) CoT 40.83, LTM 39.17, COMP 54.17, CoT+SC 40.00, COMP+SC 55.83.
limits: Column labels not recoverable from the PDF text. Paper itself says models still fall short of humans.
agent_relevance: Scaffold gains persist on perturbed variants, but plain CoT or voting does nothing for question-doubting variants (if the column reading is right); a verify-each-subgoal step did.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: what matters
finding: Invalid reasoning in demonstrations keeps over 80-90% of CoT's gain; removing relevance or coherence destroys it. So a prompt of equal length with wrong but on-topic steps is not a placebo.
numbers: text-davinci-002, first column (probably GSM8K; header lost): CoT 43.9, invalid reasoning 39.8, no coherence 25.2, no relevance 9.6. Other columns not decoded. Standard prompting 15.4 and 20.6 in two columns.
quote: invalid reasoning steps can achieve over 80-90% of the performance of CoT
limits: Table dump garbled; four LLMs; arithmetic and multi-hop QA.
agent_relevance: A true control must be off-topic and incoherent; wrong-but-relevant scaffolds still transfer format and topic. Separates format effect from content effect.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations
finding: Replacing gold labels in demonstrations with random labels barely hurts across 12 models, so much of few-shot gain is format and label-space exposure.
numbers: 12 models including GPT-3; classification and multi-choice tasks; only the abstract and figure labels were read, no per-task numbers.
limits: Read abstract and figure captions only. Classification, not reasoning.
agent_relevance: Expectation-like effect: format alone buys much of the gain, so the placebo arm must keep format fixed and vary content.

source: Pfau, Merrill & Bowman (2024) Let's Think Dot by Dot
finding: Meaningless filler tokens can give the compute benefit of chain of thought, but only in small models trained with dense supervision.
numbers: Synthetic 3SUM and 2SUM-Transform: Llama-style transformers reach 100% and 94% with filler tokens while failing without filler.
limits: Small models trained from scratch on synthetic tasks; no evidence for prompting frontier models with filler.
agent_relevance: Length-matched filler is a cheap token-count control, but for prompted frontier models it is not known to help; use it only as a floor.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: experience-following
finding: Adding every execution to memory lowers success below a fixed small memory; a strict filter (ground-truth check) raises it. Agents copy the most similar stored record, so errors spread.
numbers: Four agents. RegAgent success: fixed 67.53, add-all 55.48, coarse C1 63.18, C3 67.35, strict 70.95. EHRAgent accuracy: fixed 16.75, add-all 13.05, strict 38.50. AgentDriver: fixed 40.11, add-all 32.32, strict 51.00. CIC-IoT: fixed 71.50, add-all 59.90, strict 85.40. Memory sizes: strict 904-2938 records vs add-all 1050-4100.
limits: Strict evaluator uses ground truth (oracle), not available at deploy. Not reasoning benchmarks; mixed agent tasks.
agent_relevance: Closes gap 5: unfiltered accumulation hurts by 4 to 12 points in 4 of 4 agents; quality of what is stored matters more than quantity.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) memory deletion strategies
finding: Pruning rule that works: delete a record when its later retrieval counts and the quality of the tasks it was retrieved for are low (history-based), combined with periodic deletion for size. Fine-tuned judges are stable; an untuned GPT-4o-mini judge helped EHRAgent but hurt AgentDriver.
numbers: Coarse C1 rows: AgentDriver no-deletion 78.10 (355 records) vs history-based 68.80 (352); RegAgent history-based 59.32 (951 records) vs no-deletion about 60.88 (1012). Columns garbled, so cell assignment is uncertain.
limits: Table garbled; direction per agent uncertain; the paper says history-based deletion gives the best performance with a strict evaluator and combined deletion shrinks memory most.
agent_relevance: Prune by downstream utility of a lesson, not by age alone; rely on a reliable judge, otherwise pruning can hurt.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet, limitations section
finding: Own limitations: poor retrieval can confuse the model on diverse queries (GPT-4o dipped on GPQA-Diamond); small models (GPT-4o-mini) gain little; R1 and o1 reasoning models gave minimal or inconsistent gains; separate memories per topic are suggested but not tested.
numbers: Tokens per AIME 2024 question for Claude Sonnet: baseline 370, DC-empty 494, DC-RS 1035, DC-Cu 1831. Full history 26.7% vs 50.0% for DC on AIME 2024.
quote: separate curated memories for topics like combinatorics or physics
limits: Authors' discussion, no ablation. Keyed-versus-shared memory is explicitly future work.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open: the only direct statement is that topic-keyed memory is untested. Memory also costs tokens (about 5x at DC-Cu) and gives little for reasoning models.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank, Mind2Web Table 3 (Gemini-2.5-flash)
finding: Memory gain does not shrink steadily with distance. Step success rate (SSR) gain is similar across cross-task, cross-website and cross-domain, and AWM falls below no-memory in cross-domain.
numbers: SSR cross-task / cross-website / cross-domain: no memory 40.3 / 31.7 / 31.9; AWM 41.0 / 31.7 / 30.1; ReasoningBank 44.9 / 33.9 / 36.6 (gain +4.6 / +2.2 / +4.7). Whole-task SR: 3.3->4.8, 1.7->2.3, 1.0->1.6.
limits: Web tasks, not reasoning; one model in this row; whole-task SR is tiny so differences are noisy; no confidence intervals.
agent_relevance: Corrects K17: ReasoningBank gain is not monotone with distance; AWM-style workflow memory is what degrades far away.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank, Mind2Web Table 3 (Gemini-2.5-pro)
finding: With the larger model, ReasoningBank's step-success gain rises with distance.
numbers: SSR cross-task / website / domain: no memory 44.4 / 34.8 / 35.0; AWM 44.4 / 34.8 / 34.4; ReasoningBank 45.6 / 36.9 / 38.1 (gain +1.2 / +2.1 / +3.1). Whole-task SR 3.5->5.1, 3.4->3.8, 1.4->1.7.
limits: Same limits as d13. Distance here is website/domain, not problem class on reasoning tasks.
agent_relevance: Abstracted strategy items can transfer farther than raw workflows; still no reasoning-task distance curve exists.

source: arXiv 2505.00603 (2025) Can LLMs aid analogical reasoning for strategic decisions? humans vs GPT-4 (Gick-Holyoak adapted)
finding: Gick-Holyoak style test adapted to a matching task (two sources, two targets). With no hint GPT-4 almost never picked the correct source; with a hint recall was perfect but half of claims were false positives.
numbers: GPT-4 60 trials (15 per cell). No hint: used an analogy 1/15 on the radiation-based factory problem and 14/15 on the dolphin-based HR problem, yet correct-source precision and recall were 0.00 in both. With hint: radiation TP 15 FN 0 FP 14 TN 1, precision 0.52, recall 1.00, accuracy 0.53; dolphin precision 0.50, accuracy 0.50. Humans N=199: solved factory 6.3% no hint vs 8.7% hint (4/46), HR 20.3% vs about 37% (17/46); human precision 0.50-0.75, recall 0.26-0.39 with hint.
limits: Not an exact replication; the hint makes the existence of an analogy explicit. The paper's own measures differ between 'used any analogy' and 'used the correct one'. GPT-4 only; one prompt.
agent_relevance: Partly answers gap 6. A hint raises reuse but also false matches, so a stored lesson needs a match check, not only a cue.

source: Gick & Holyoak (1983) Experiment 2 as cited in arXiv 2505.00603
finding: Second-hand human baseline: spontaneous use of the analogy was 29% (8/28) and 50% (14/28) with a hint in Experiment 2.
numbers: 8/28 vs 14/28; compare 6.3-8.7% and 20.3-37% in the 2025 adaptation.
limits: Read only as cited in 2505.00603; the original 1980 and 1983 papers were not opened. The often quoted 10-30% vs about 90% pair is therefore still unverified.
agent_relevance: Human no-hint to hint rise is real but 1983 Experiment 2 shows 29 to 50%, not 20-30 to 90%; do not quote them as one study.

source: Press et al. (2022) Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
finding: Models answer both sub-questions of a 2-hop question yet fail to compose them; the gap stays at roughly 40% as models scale. Explicit decomposition (self-ask) with a search engine narrows it.
numbers: davinci-002 exact match (Table 14): 2WikiMultiHopQA direct 25.4, CoT 29.8, self-ask 30.0, self-ask + search 40.1; Musique direct 5.6, CoT 12.6, self-ask 13.8, self-ask + search 15.2. Bamboogle with search about 57.6-60.0 (Table 1 garbled).
limits: GPT-3 era. Does not test current reasoning models or tools; decomposition gave +4.4 to +14.7 EM points, not full rescue.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 only partly answered: decomposition and retrieval help older models; no frontier-with-tools measurement found.

source: Abrami et al. (2015), re-read for what the 0.57 means (Clearing House Unterricht summary)
finding: The 0.57 is an outcome-type split: effect on content-specific critical-thinking measures, not teaching content-specifically. Overall g=0.30 is stable across subject matter, age and duration; explicit versus infused teaching did not differ significantly; STEM vs non-STEM did not differ significantly.
numbers: g=0.30 (341 effects); content-specific CT outcome 0.57 (97); disposition 0.23 (25); subject facts 0.33 (140); combined three approaches 0.57 (19); ages 11-15 0.37 vs 16-18 0.25, not significant. Stage 1 selected studies using moderator analyses of design type and test instrument.
quote: It did not play a significant role whether it was taught explicitly ... or in combination with concrete lesson content.
limits: Secondary summary; the SAGE PDF returned 403. Control type and design quality were screening criteria in stage 1, not reported as moderators of the 0.57.
agent_relevance: Abrami does not show that domain-bound teaching beats general teaching. It supports: tests close to the taught content show bigger gains (a transfer-distance effect).

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Critical Thinking, methods supplement (Abrami figures)
finding: Reports four approaches with effect sizes and says the mixed advantage was not statistically significant.
numbers: Mixed (general plus infusion or immersion) +0.38; infusion +0.29; general +0.26; immersion +0.23; overall 0.30 across 341 effect sizes ranging from -1 to +2.
limits: Attribution to the 2015 paper was not independently checked (page fetched through a summariser). Design-quality effect sizes not given.
agent_relevance: Content-embedded (infusion/immersion) is not clearly better than general instruction: spread between best and worst is 0.15, not significant.

source: Abrami et al. (2015) primary paper, access attempt
finding: Primary PDF returned HTTP 403; abstract confirmed through a repository record: 341 effect sizes, g+ = 0.30, p < .001, dialogue, authentic problems and mentoring helped.
numbers: g+ 0.30 only.
limits: No moderator table seen, so whether any advantage survives control-type and quality modelling stays open.
agent_relevance: Cannot cite moderator-adjusted effects. Treat as unresolved.
